epithet: Has the time not come for hearts to be humbled?
lede: A surah for believers who have grown comfortable. It opens with some of the most majestic lines ever spoken about Allah, and then asks those who say they believe in Him to prove it — with their wealth, with their hearts, and with iron.

names.name: al-Ḥadīd
names.note: After the iron of its twenty-fifth ayah, sent down “with great might in it, and benefits for people”. It is the first of the Musabbiḥāt, the surahs that open with the glorification of Allah.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī gives it as Madinan from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, Jābir ibn Zayd, Qatādah and Muqātil, and records one saying, from al-Kalbī, that it is Makkan; al-Qurṭubī calls it Madinan in the saying of all. Its tenth ayah speaks of the Opening as something that has already happened — “those of you who spent and fought before the Opening are not equal” — which places that passage after al-Ḥudaybiyah or the conquest of Makkah. A report from Ibn Masʿūd in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim suggests that ayah 16 is earlier.
revelation.when: Madinah, after the Opening — when Islam had become safe to join, and cheap

evidence.quote: وَفِيها قَوْلانِ أحَدُهُما: أنَّها مَدَنِيَّةٌ، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وبِهِ قالَ الحَسَنُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وجابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، وقَتادَةُ، ومُقاتِلٌ. والثّانِي: أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ السّائِبِ
سورة الحديد مَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَهِيَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ آيَةً

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «الحَدِيدِ» بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: For the first Muslims, belief had cost everything: homes, property, family, sometimes life. By the time this surah came down that had changed. The community had a city and an army; after the Opening it was the winning side. People were entering Islam who had risked nothing for it, and some who had been in it for years had begun to hold on to what they owned.

The surah speaks to that moment. It begins far above it — everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward; He is with you wherever you are — and then comes down to a blunt request: believe, and spend out of what He has made you trustees of. It draws a line no later generosity can cross: those who spent and fought before the Opening are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards, though Allah has promised the best to all.

Then the question that gives the surah its edge. “Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should be humbled at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth, and that they not be like those given the Scripture before, for whom the time grew long, so their hearts grew hard?” Ibn Masʿūd said: between our accepting Islam and Allah reproaching us with this ayah there were only four years.

Its closing passages name what a community needs. Messengers, with the Book and the Balance, so that people may stand by justice. And iron — in which there is great might — so that Allah may make known who will help Him and His messengers, unseen.

occasions.title: Four years
occasions.text: “There were only four years between our accepting Islam and Allah reproaching us with this ayah: ‘Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should be humbled at the remembrance of Allah?’”

aim: To build the strength of faith and of means that drives a people to call to Allah and to strive — and to free souls from what holds them back; which is why spending and belief are mentioned in it again and again.
themes: The names and majesty of Allah

outline.title: Who He is
outline.summary: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah. His is the dominion; He gives life and causes death. He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and He knows all things. He created the heavens and the earth in six days and then rose over the Throne; He knows what enters the earth and what leaves it, what descends from the sky and what ascends — and He is with you wherever you are.

outline.title: Believe, and spend
outline.summary: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from what He has made you successors in. What ails you that you do not spend in Allah’s way, when to Him belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the Opening. Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, that He may multiply it for him?

outline.title: The light, and the wall
outline.summary: The Day you see the believing men and women with their light streaming before them and on their right. The hypocrites will call to them: “Wait for us, that we may take from your light.” A wall is set between them with a gate in it: mercy within, punishment without. “Were we not with you?” — “Yes; but you led yourselves into temptation, and waited, and doubted, and false hopes deceived you.”

outline.title: Has the time not come?
outline.summary: Has the time not come for the hearts of those who believe to be humbled at the remembrance of Allah, and not be like those before them whose hearts hardened with the passing of time? Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. Those who give in charity, men and women, will have it multiplied; and those who believe in Allah and His messengers — they are the truthful, and the witnesses with their Lord.

outline.title: What this life is
outline.summary: Know that the life of this world is play and diversion and adornment, boasting among yourselves and rivalry in wealth and children — like a rain whose growth delights the sowers, then withers, yellows and turns to chaff. So race towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the sky and the earth. No misfortune strikes on earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before We bring it into being — so that you do not grieve over what has passed you by, nor exult over what He has given you.

outline.title: The Book, the Balance and iron
outline.summary: We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice; and We sent down iron, in which is great might and benefits for people. We sent Nūḥ and Ibrāhīm, and placed prophethood and the Book among their descendants; then ʿĪsā son of Maryam, and gave him the Gospel. The monasticism his followers invented, We did not prescribe for them.

outline.title: A double share
outline.summary: O you who believe: be mindful of Allah and believe in His Messenger, and He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and make for you a light to walk by, and forgive you — so that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over any of Allah’s bounty; it is in His hand, and He gives it to whom He wills.

keyAyah.why: The surah’s question, put to believers and not to deniers. A heart can harden simply by the passing of time.

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite the Musabbiḥāt before he lay down to sleep, and would say: “In them is an ayah that is better than a thousand ayat.” The Musabbiḥāt are the surahs that open with the glorification of Allah; al-Ḥadīd is the first of them, and Ibn Kathīr takes the ayah to be its third: “He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward.”

Of the supplication of the Prophet ﷺ on going to bed: “O Allah, You are the First, and there is nothing before You; You are the Last, and there is nothing after You; You are the Outward, and there is nothing above You; You are the Inward, and there is nothing nearer than You. Settle our debt for us, and free us from poverty.”
virtues.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَيْءٌ

before: Al-Wāqiʿah closed with a command: glorify the name of your Lord, the Tremendous. Al-Ḥadīd opens with the news that everything already does.
after: Al-Ḥadīd ends by saying that Allah’s bounty is in His hand, and that He knows what is in every heart. Al-Mujādilah opens with one woman’s complaint, spoken low in a corner of a room, that He heard.
